### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/page.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via emptyState (symbol, a field of const object RecordDetailsProps, an authorable key of ui/RecordDetailsProps; a field of const object RecordHighlightsProps, an authorable key of ui/RecordHighlightsProps; a field of const object RecordQuickActionsProps, an authorable key of ui/RecordQuickActionsProps))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via emptyState (symbol, a field of const object RecordDetailsProps, an authorable key of ui/RecordDetailsProps; a field of const object RecordHighlightsProps, an authorable key of ui/RecordHighlightsProps; a field of const object RecordQuickActionsProps, an authorable key of ui/RecordQuickActionsProps))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/page.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `534cc5a24e1279f14d4e708605c31a45c30479bf` — the merge of head `40ef667d2a16185313b7508e839197e59789014c` into base `53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 534cc5a24e1279f14d4e708605c31a45c30479bf && git checkout 534cc5a24e1279f14d4e708605c31a45c30479bf
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69 40ef667d2a16185313b7508e839197e59789014c && git checkout -B drift-repro 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69 && git merge --no-ff 40ef667d2a16185313b7508e839197e59789014c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `40ef667d2a16185313b7508e839197e59789014c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts (`EmptyStateSchema`, `emptyStateLinkSchema`), packages/spec/src/ui/component-record-blocks-empty-state-24266.test.ts, packages/spec/liveness/page.json, packages/spec/scripts/liveness/check-liveness.mts (`MARKER_RE`), packages/spec/scripts/liveness/empty-state.mts, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json with packages/spec/scripts/lib/dropped-refinements.ts and packages/spec/scripts/dropped-refinements.test.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json, .changeset/24266-record-blocks-empty-state.md, content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx, packages/lint/src/validate-component-props.ts, and objectui `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/recordBinding.tsx` plus its three call sites at objectui `main` `79cb8c03eb` and at the console pin `5e15928b46`. Remainder at TIER_DEFAULT: none — every path of the diff was read here.

Inputs: card #24266 (body, claim 6246456531, report 6246857118), PR #24270 (body, 7-file list, net diff against `main` `53ef7524`; merge-base `a422f04f`), the check-runs on the head. The head had not moved when read (`ls-remote` answers `40ef667d`). The precedents named by the card and the dev were read in the cited code: `ObjectGridPropsSchema.emptyState` (#20694) and `RecordRelatedListProps.parentDataSource` (#23134).

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the cited code:

1. `RecordDetailsProps`, `RecordHighlightsProps`, `RecordQuickActionsProps` each accept an optional `emptyState` — **right**. All three are `strictObject`s with no `emptyState` on `main` (the card's premise, H1, holds). The member is `EmptyStateSchema.optional().describe(...)`, the same import `object-grid.emptyState` already uses (`component.zod.ts:28`), so the shape is by reference, not re-spelled — the card's one hard constraint. §3 of the pin proves it by def identity against both `EmptyStateSchema` and `ObjectGridPropsSchema.shape.emptyState`.
2. No fourth block — **right**. At objectui `main` `79cb8c03eb` and at the pin `5e15928b46`, `recordBindingBlock` has exactly three call sites (`record-details.tsx`, `record-highlights.tsx`, `record-quick-actions.tsx`). `record:related_list` binds its parent through `ParentRecordBinding`, whose `absent` node is the declared 0-row answer; the pin's per-type door (§2, last case) keeps `emptyState` refused there. Matches the card ("a fourth is added only if … bound the same way").
3. The describe's condition — **right against the card and the renderer**. The card requires "drawn when the block's bound `dataSource` yields no row, and only then"; the describe says exactly that ("Drawn then and only then — never on a block with no `dataSource` …, never while the bound read is loading, and never in place of the error a failed read shows"). `recordBinding.tsx` confirms the three arms: unbound renders children as they are (record page path); `dataSource && !current` draws the loading skeleton; `status === 'failed'` draws `ElementDataSourceErrorPanel`; a settled read with no row mounts a record context with no record — the one state the key names. The `record:quick_actions` clause ("a bound record whose bar resolves no action keeps the empty placeholder") correctly separates a 0-row binding from a row with no actions. One nuance is carried in the TSDoc rather than the author-facing describe — see ③ flag 1.
4. Nothing else in the file moves — **right**. The describe constant `BOUND_RECORD_BLOCK_EMPTY_STATE_DESCRIPTION` is module-private, the same way `RECORD_BLOCK_REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS_DESCRIPTION` is; no export is added, removed or renamed, so `check:api-surface` has nothing to regenerate. No guidance or retired-key map on these rows, on `PageComponentSchema`, or anywhere in `packages/spec/src` names `emptyState` for these blocks (the only other `emptyState:` alias is on a translation shape in `system/translation.zod.ts`, unrelated), so the widening contradicts no standing prescription.
5. Lint (`os validate`) follows without a change — **right**. `packages/lint/src/validate-component-props.ts` reads `ComponentPropsMap` (`PROPS_SCHEMAS = ComponentPropsMap`) and reports unknown keys through `lintUnknownKeysAgainstSchema`, so the three rows now accept `emptyState` and every other row still reports `component-props-unknown-key`, as the changeset says.
6. Authorable surface — **right**. `authorable-surface/ui.json` gains exactly `ui/RecordDetailsProps:emptyState`, `ui/RecordHighlightsProps:emptyState`, `ui/RecordQuickActionsProps:emptyState`, each in sorted position; nothing else moves.
7. Dropped-refinements ledger — **right, and owed**. `EmptyStateSchema.link` is `emptyStateLinkSchema()` whose `url` rule is a refinement that does not project; `ui/ObjectGridProps` and `ui/ListView` already declare `emptyState.link.url` for the same reason. The diff adds that site under the three rows and moves the two reconciled counts: entries 236 to 238 (`RecordDetailsProps` already had a row for `sections.element`, so only two schemas are new) and sites 767 to 770. Both equal what `dropped-refinements.test.ts` pins (`measured.publishedSchemasWithDroppedRefinements` equals `entries.length`). The ledger's own text says a new site fails `build-schemas.ts` until the line moves, so this hand edit is the prescribed act, not a surface breach (deviation 4 below).
8. Liveness — **right, by the precedent the dev names**. The describe opens with `[PLANNED — not yet rendered]`, which `check-liveness.mts` `MARKER_RE.planned` (`/\[planned|…/i`) grades as `planned`; §4 of the pin holds the marker at position 0. A component-level key carries no ledger row (the walk stops at the undrilled `page/regions` container), so the record is the `page.json` `_note` PLANNED RECORD sentence, which carries the same members as the #23134 sentence: the key path, the schema and file, the objectui measurement sha and consumer path, the carrier (objectstack-ai/objectui#12932), why no row carries it, the checkable rows, and the rewrite condition. The `Spec property liveness` check-run on this head is green. Declaring ahead of the renderer is the card's own order ("objectui#12932 dispatches once this key is in the spec installs"), and the marker plus the `_note` keep Prime Directive 10's declared-vs-enforced line visible; this is the same shape #23134 landed under.
9. `check:empty-state` — **no exposure read**. The new prose contains no `empty-ish ... = / means / → ... permissive` statement and no `leave empty to …` imperative ("Omitted, a binding with no row keeps the block's own placeholder" names a non-permissive consequence with no separator token), so the pure-source audit has nothing new to classify. CI's verdict on it is the gate's, not mine.
10. Docs — **generated, consistent**. `content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx` gains the three `emptyState` rows and three nested-shape tables whose text equals the describes; the Docs Drift Check's two release-page rows (`v17/17-6`, `17-7`) are advisory and read-only, and nothing here edits them.
11. Console pin — **no break possible**. A widening of three strict props cannot refuse anything the pinned objectui (`5e15928b46`) authors today, and nothing at the pin reads the key.

Measurements the PR claims that I re-read in code: H1 (premise), H2 (three call sites, both shas), H4 (lint derives from `ComponentPropsMap`) — each holds. The ablation claim (one line removed, 6 cases red, blob restored to HEAD) is the dev's run and is consistent with the pin's shape (per block: 3 of §1, 3 of §2 — one of which still passes on a missing key — §3 and §4 ≈ 6 reds); not re-run here.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/24266-record-blocks-empty-state.md` declares `"@objectstack/spec": minor` and carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` as a bare line; the PR body carries the identical line at the start of a line, the one carrier `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads. The diff publishes exactly one thing from a released package: three published Zod props objects each accept one new optional key. Nothing narrows, no key or export is removed or renamed, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed (that line is for breaking changesets) and no migration text is owed. `minor` is the floor for `yes` and the right level here; `skip-changeset` would be wrong. The card body asked for `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and a `minor` changeset — matched. `Check Changeset` on this head is green.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — judged right.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (report 6246857118), each answered:

- Deviation 1 (local worktree branch spelled `…-wt`, pushes via `HEAD:refspec` to the claimed remote name): accepted. The remote branch is `claude/issue-24266-record-blocks-empty-state`, the PR head is that ref, and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` is green.
- Deviation 2 (WIP commits pushed without the trailer pair, then squashed with `--force-with-lease=branch:6caf1d6d` before any PR existed): accepted on what is still observable. The branch carries one commit beyond `main`, author and committer are one identity, the commit (06:56:32Z) predates the PR (06:58:32Z), the name is `claude/issue-*`, and the lease form was the spelled one. The pre-squash history cannot be re-read; the five criteria are taken on the report plus these readings.
- Deviation 3 (harness attribution vs AGENTS.md: model-free trailer pair, session-URL PR footer): accepted — AGENTS.md is the rule that binds here; the head commit ends with `Claude-Session:` and a model-free `Co-authored-by:`, the PR body footer is the session-URL form, and no model identifier appears in the title, body, changeset or code.
- Deviation 4 (`dropped-refinements.baseline.json` hand-edited outside the named file surface): accepted — see ① item 7. The ledger is hand-edited by design, has no generator, and refuses the build until the new sites are declared; the three sites are the same `emptyState.link.url` refinement `ui/ObjectGridProps` declares. This is the one edit the surface could not have named in advance.

`open_questions`: none declared; none found.

Out-of-scope finding (carrier none; `measured.refinementSitesThatDidProject` reads 369 while the build prints 467): answered, not a blocker. That field has no reader anywhere in the repository — `dropped-refinements.test.ts` pins only `publishedSchemasWithDroppedRefinements` and `droppedRefinementSites`, and `build-schemas.ts` prints the projected count without comparing it — so it is a hand-maintained number nothing measures, already stale on `main` and untouched by this diff. It is a ledger-hygiene defect of the declared-but-unreconciled kind: the owning seat should file it as a small tooling card (pin the field in the test the way the other two are, or drop it) rather than leave it as prose. Not this PR's to fix.

Reviewer flags for the carrier, not FAIL reasons:

1. Forbidden reads. `recordBinding.tsx` classifies a server-refused read as `loaded` with no row ("absent" and "not yours to read" are indistinguishable there), so under the declared condition the authored `emptyState` will be drawn for a forbidden read too. The TSDoc above `BOUND_RECORD_BLOCK_EMPTY_STATE_DESCRIPTION` states this; the author-facing describe does not. That is consistent with the renderer as it stands and with the card's wording, and it is the contract objectstack-ai/objectui#12932 must keep: if the renderer half ever separates the two, the describe gains the clause in the same PR.
2. Check-runs on the head, read twice. At 06:59Z: 22 completed (17 success, 5 skipped), 16 in progress. At 07:08Z: 39 runs, 31 completed (26 success, 5 skipped, 0 failures) — green now include `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, every `Lint ·` lane, `Type Check · source gates` (the spec `check:generated` family) and `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs` — and 8 still in progress: `Test Core` 1–6, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record judges the contract and does not wait on them. The surface is not governed (0 of 7 paths), so the owning seat lands it through the queue once every check is green.

Reviewed-by: `session_01TyRhWbVbbQpQJTDbW8VahJ`
